thread:
sara-ng: Hey folks — first day! Trying to get my devcontainer working on Windows (WSL2 + Docker). asdf installs fine but yarn/npm keep failing during native modules build. I suspect proxy/env vars. Anyone seen this?

mariela: welcome! quick q: are you on corp VPN or behind the company proxy?

sara-ng: I'm on my home network but company VPN (wireguard) is connected. I noticed `npm install` times out to registry sometimes. Also `brew` in WSL2 container isn't present — using asdf-managed node/ruby.

devon: from memory, the devcontainers we use set HTTP(S)_PROXY in your devcontainer.json if the host has a proxy. Check `env` in the container.

sara-ng: good call. ran `env | grep -i proxy` inside container: nothing. In the host powershell I have `HTTP_PROXY` set for some other tools.

mariela: devcontainer usually doesn't automatically copy host env unless allowed. We add a few to .devcontainer/devcontainer.json like: "remoteEnv": { "HTTP_PROXY": "${localEnv:HTTP_PROXY}" } — but be careful with secrets.

sara-ng: ah that explains it. can't edit company repo template yet. any quick workaround?

devon: you can temporarily export in the shell: `export HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.company:8080` and `export HTTPS_PROXY=$HTTP_PROXY`. also set `npm config set proxy http://proxy.company:8080` and `npm config set https-proxy http://proxy.company:8080`.

sara-ng: tried that, but node-gyp still fails with `gyp ERR! find VS` stuff. stack trace mentions Python and `msbuild`. I assume native build expects Windows toolchain?

mariela: for WSL2 containers, compile happens inside Linux container. Ensure you have `build-essential` and `python3` in the container image. We have helper script in repo `scripts/setup-dev.sh` that installs apt deps.

sara-ng: I ran apt deps. The error seems to be complaining about the `node-gyp` MSVC binder because some packages prefer Windows toolchain when `process.platform` is detected incorrectly? weird.

devon: hmm. can you paste the failing lines? small snippets are fine.

sara-ng: stack snippet: ```
error: gyp: No Xcode or CLT version detected
make: *** [binding.target.mk:99: Release/obj.target/some_native_module/src/native.o] Error 2
```

mariela: that message looks macOS-specific — are you sure the container image is linux and not accidentally using macOS base?

sara-ng: ooooh I noticed my asdf node install was using `nodejs` from host via vol-mounted `~/.asdf` and the binary was Darwin one? I had mounted home dir and that included host-tooling.

devon: ah yes — avoid mounting host-built binaries into linux container. Two fixes: rebuild node inside container using asdf there, or mount only `~/.asdf/installs` selectively. We usually recommend installing runtimes inside the container.

sara-ng: doing `asdf install nodejs 18.17.1` inside container now. Also removed the host PATH mount. Thanks!

infra-bot: FYI: if you're on an M1/M2 host and running linux containers, some precompiled host artifacts can leak in via shared volumes — see infra doc: https://internal.redwood/infra/containers#host-artifacts

mariela: once node is local, also `npm rebuild` the module. and if you still hit network timeouts, add `--fetch-retries=5` and `--verbose` to see registry URLs.

sara-ng: success! node installed in-container, npm install finished. Two follow-ups: 1) where do we put notes about updating devcontainer.json for proxies? 2) who to ping for 1Password CLI access to fetch creds?

devon: 1) open a tiny PR against repo's `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` and link this thread — keep it opt-in with a commented example. 2) ping infra on #eng-infra or email infra@redwood.com for 1Password team provisioning. cc @mariela can help with immediate temp token if needed.

sara-ng: thanks all! adding the quick PR now. :rocket:
